maya: Quick thought — can we stop using a strict tier -> variant mapping and instead shape routing with a per-request token budget? cheaper fallback only when estimated cost would push the customer over credit thresholds.
jon: hmm interesting. So instead of `tier=pro -> model=A`, we do `if est_cost > budget -> route(model=B)` ?
li: that avoids punting low-cost bursts but still protects monthly commit. Sounds sensible. How do we estimate cost before routing though?
taylor: we already have size_estimator that looks at prompt length + expected completion length. Add model_token_rate (tokens/sec) or token_price to compute est_cost. cheap check is O(1).
maya: exactly. sketch: 
```
est_tokens = prompt_tokens + expected_completion_tokens
est_cost = est_tokens * variant_unit_price
if est_cost > remaining_credit * refund_safe_factor:
  route_to = cheap_variant
else:
  route_to = preferred_variant
```
jon: wallet/credits are per-account and per-sku, plus reserved capacity. Need to include reserved_capacity_safety so we don't shift high-SLA customers to cheap variants if they have dedicated capacity.
li: telemetry ask: we need a new signal `routing.decision_reason` with values: budget_shaping, capacity_fallback, manual_override, routing_policy. Also log `est_cost`, `remaining_credit`, `variant_chosen`.
platform-bot: Deploy checklist reminder: add unit tests for estimator, integration test for route decision, and a console toggle for rolling out the shaping policy.
taylor: console UX: in customer view add a small panel: 
- current_month_credits_remaining
- configured_budget_shaping (on/off)
- safety_threshold (percent)
so support can flip shaping off per-customer.
maya: rollout plan: A/B to 5% of low-tier customers, capture conversion/drop/retry rates, and token spend delta. Canary in region us-west-2 first.
jon: internal API debate: Should shaping live in routing-service (fast path) or in the policy-engine (centralized)? Fast path reduces latency but duplicates credit lookup code. Policy-engine centralizes rules but adds RPC.
li: propose hybrid: cache credit windows in routing-service with TTL and a signed/nonce check from policy-engine for overrides. That keeps common case fast.
taylor: rollback/guard: if cheap_variant error rate > 1.5x baseline for 10m, auto-disable shaping for that variant and send alert. opsbot will create an incident if consumers drop > 5% success rate.
maya: telemetry KPIs to track: token_spend_delta, requests_routed_to_cheap_pct, avg_latency_by_variant, failed_requests_by_variant, customer_churn_signal (coarse).
jon: small nit: include a per-request annotation for billing_reason so billing can attribute actual cost and we can run post-hoc audits.
li: I'll draft the proto for the routing RPC and example console mockups. Maya/Taylor can I get your input on the UX copy and safety defaults?
maya: yes, will review. thanks — want this in next sprint planning if we agree on hybrid approach.
platform-bot: Note: feature-flag key `feature:budget-shaping-routing` created for gradual rollout.
